chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)

That he was asked about a man who enters the mosque and fears that the ruku' (bowing) will be missed, so he said: 'He bows before he reaches the congregation, and walks while he is bowing until he reaches them.'

key_terms.اَلرَّكْعَةُ: The bowing position in Islamic prayer
key_terms.وَهُوَ رَاكِعٌ: And he is in the bowing state

ai.seo_question: How should a person join the prayer if they are late and fear missing the ruku'?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical jurisprudence of joining a late prayer, emphasizing the validity of the individual's independent ruku' before merging with the congregation. It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on maintaining the physical integrity of the prayer unit even when entering late, ensuring the worshipper does not miss the essential pillar of bowing. This method preserves the communal aspect of the prayer while accommodating the individual's delayed entry.
